_note: These default rules are a working hypothesis. The call order an input method engine follows is not documented by the operating system, nor is the sequence of calls that signals a cancellation (on macOS, unmarkText is treated as a commit signal). Revise the rules against the call sequences observed on calibration-pilot devices. Schema of a rule set: start is the event that opens a composition; commit and cancel are arrays of events that close a composition; candidate is the event taken to indicate that a candidate window has appeared (unavailable on macOS, hence null); candidate_end is the event taken to indicate that a candidate window has closed (same schema as candidate; also null on macOS); clock_jump_ms is the threshold for a clock discontinuity. For win_tsf, the tsf_end event may omit result_len; when omitted, after_result is treated as false and the event is counted as a cancellation. Confirm this against a reference-input-field implementation in which the composition-end callback does not report the length of the committed result.
